subject: Gray Wolfos
text: A Gray Wolfos can be killed in one shot by backflipping to dodge its attack when it moves close, then immediately landing and performing a Jump Attack while its back is turned.

evidence.quote: The easiest method to defeat the Gray Wolfos (or any Wolfos, for that matter) is to stand still, and wait for them to move in close.  Just as they attack, perform a back flip (Back + A while Z-Targeted) to dodge their attack, then immediately after you land perform a Jump Attack (press A while Z-targeted).  The Wolfos will briefly have his back turned to you, and the Jump Attack will kill it in one shot.

subject: Sacred Forest Meadow Gate
text: Defeating the Gray Wolfos causes the gate blocking the entrance to the Sacred Forest Meadow to disappear.

evidence.quote: When the Gray Wolfos dies, the gate blocking the entrance to the Sacred Forest Meadow will disappear, letting you in.

subject: Saria's Song
text: At the top of the stairs in a small overgrown courtyard, Saria teaches Link Saria's Song.

evidence.quote: At the top, you will find Saria sitting in a small, overgrown courtyard.  Saria will now teach you Saria's Song, which brings happiness to the depressed, and allows you to communicate telepathically with Saria at any time.

subject: Fairy Fountain
text: A Fairy Fountain is located in the pit in the middle of the upper cliffs area of the Sacred Forest Meadow.

evidence.quote: The pit in the middle of the upper cliffs area contains a Fairy Fountain if you need Life.

subject: Piece of Heart
text: Playing Saria's Song for the Skullkid standing on a small trunk in the Lost Woods rewards a Piece of Heart.

evidence.quote: Go left through the hollowed log, and jump onto the small trunk to interact with the Skullkid (and yes, this is the same Skullkid who unwittingly becomes the villain in Majora's Mask).  Play Saria's Song for the Scarecrow Kid, and he'll give you a Piece of Heart (which should get you another complete Heart Container).

subject: Kakariko Village
text: The entrance to Kakariko Village is in the northeast corner of Hyrule Field.

evidence.quote: We're now going to take Impa's advice and head for Kakariko Village, whose entrance is in the very northeast corner of Hyrule Field (1:00 on the  clock face).

subject: Bottle
text: Gathering all the Cuccos scattered around Kakariko Village and returning them to the Cucco Lady's pasture rewards a Bottle.

evidence.quote: The first order of business in Kakariko is to gather up all the Cuccos around town and deliver them to the Cucco Lady, who will give you a Bottle for your trouble.

subject: Cucco #1
text: A Cucco is found running near the archway at the front entrance of Kakariko Village.

evidence.quote: Run forward through the arch in front of the town, and immediately grab the Cucco (chicken) who is running around here.

subject: Cucco #2
text: A Cucco is located near the Cucco Lady's pasture, close to the arch leading to the Graveyard in the southeast corner of town.

evidence.quote: Grab the next Cucco very near the Cucco Lady's pasture, near the arch leading to the Graveyard in the southeast corner.

subject: Cucco #3
text: A Cucco is inside a crate near the center of town across from the stairs leading to the upper level.

evidence.quote: The next Cucco is in a crate near the center of town, across from the stairs leading to the upper level of Kakariko.

subject: Cucco #4
text: A Cucco is located on the north upper level of town near the gate leading to Death Mountain.

evidence.quote: The next Cucco is on the north side of town, on the upper level, near the gate that leads to Death Mountain.

subject: Cucco #5
text: To reach the Cucco trapped on a fenced ledge near the large tree, jump from the stairs of the partially constructed building toward the ledge while holding another Cucco to float over.

evidence.quote: To reach this Cucco, climb up the stairs to the partially constructed building, and jump off the edge towards the Cucco while holding another Cucco in your hands.  The Cucco will help you float out to the ledge.

subject: Cucco #6
text: A Cucco is found running in the small grotto behind the building reached by floating with a Cucco over the elevated fenced platform from the long stairset east of the pasture.

evidence.quote: Climb up the long stairset to the east of the Cucco Lady's pasture, and run straight to the edge, and aim yourself right at the elevated platform which is fenced off...grab another Cucco running around in the small grotto behind the building.

subject: Cucco #7
text: The final Cucco is found behind the Windmill at the top of the tall ladder in the small grotto.

evidence.quote: Drop back down into the grotto, then climb the tall ladder near where you found your most recent Cucco.  Climb it all the way to the top, and work your way around behind the Windmill.  Grab the last Cucco

subject: Piece of Heart
text: Gliding with a Cucco from the narrow wooden beam onto the high balcony of Impa's House allows Link to enter a crack and collect a Piece of Heart.

evidence.quote: Run along the beam, and when you reach the corner where the beam bends to the right, leap off the edge and steer yourself right for the balcony...Throw aside the Cucco and enter the crack in the building...Take the Piece of Heart, then leave the way you came in.

subject: Gold Skulltula Token
text: Releasing a bottled bug over the soft earth patch on the left side of Kakariko Graveyard causes a Gold Skulltula to emerge.

evidence.quote: Pass under the arch then follow the stone path to the left side of the graveyard, where there is a patch of soft earth.  Stand near the patch of soft earth, and release the bug you captured (which has magically become three separate bugs)...A few seconds later, a Gold Skulltula will appear.  Kill it and take it's token

subject: Royal Family's Tomb
text: Playing Zelda's Lullaby on the Triforce symbol in front of the largest tombstone in Kakariko Graveyard causes it to explode, revealing the pit to the Royal Family's Tomb.

evidence.quote: Stand on the large Triforce symbol burned into the grass in front of the tombstone, take out your Ocarina and play Zelda's Lullaby.  The tombstone will literally explode, revealing a pit.  Drop down the pit.

subject: Bone Pit Door
text: Killing all the Keese in the bone pit room unlocks the door at the top of the stairs in the Royal Family's Tomb.

evidence.quote: Run down the ramp and run in circles around the large bone pit to attract the attention of all the Keese in the room.  Pick them off with your Slingshot or with sword attacks.  Once they are all dead, the door at the top of the stairset will unlock.

subject: Sun's Song
text: Reading the inscription on the large tomb inside the Royal Family's Tomb teaches the Sun's Song, which turns day to night and night to day.

evidence.quote: Read the inscription on the tomb to discover the notes to the Sun's Song, which turns Night into Day and Day into Night.

subject: Shield Grave
text: Pulling back the front-row gravestone that has flowers behind it at nighttime reveals a pit leading to the Shield Grave.

evidence.quote: Head for the front row of gravestones, and stand behind the grave with the flowers behind it.  Grab a hold of it, and pull back to reveal a pit beneath the gravestone...Drop down the pit.

subject: Poe
text: Pulling aside other gravestones in Kakariko Graveyard reveals Poe enemies, who turn invisible when Z-targeted.

evidence.quote: Be careful pulling aside any other gravestones - they all contain Poe enemies, who become invisible when Z-Targeted.

subject: Hylian Shield
text: Opening the treasure chest inside the Shield Grave grants the Hylian Shield, which is impervious to flame attacks.

evidence.quote: Run forward and open the chest to find the Hylian Shield...switch the Hylian Shield, whose metal is impervious to flame attacks.

subject: Sun's Song Rupee Trick
text: Climbing the chains on the Hyrule Castle entrance gate in Hyrule Field and playing the Sun's Song causes the gate to retract, allowing Link to collect four invisible red rupees worth 80 rupees.

evidence.quote: Now that you have the Sun's Song, you also have access to a quick and easy 80 rupees.  If you return to the entrance to Hyrule Castle in Hyrule Field, then climb up the chains on the gate, then you can play the Sun's Song.  The gate will retract, letting you walk along the edge of the gate to claim four invisible red rupees.  This is known as the "Sun's Song Rupee Trick," and I will reference it a few times throughout the guide.
